Docs/End effectors

End effectors

Choose among the four registered end effectors while keeping released-data coverage and joint layouts explicit.

Four variants of each task

Every task registers one environment ID for each of Sharpa, Wuji, XHand and Gripper: <Task>-<Hand>-v1. The 40 task definitions therefore register 160 environment IDs. The end-effector and robot-UID rules live in tasks/config/hands.py ↗; the task list lives in tasks/config/collection_targets.py ↗.

The 40 definitions are 10 complete tasks and their 30 stages, not 160 distinct task objectives. See task table ↗ for each task's arm side and registered horizon.

Resolve the robot for a chosen hand

from tasks.config.hands import HANDS, env_id, robot_uid

for hand in HANDS:
    print(env_id("DrawerPlugOpenDrawer", hand), robot_uid(hand, "left"))

Use left, right or both according to the task registration. Do not attach a robot from a different stage merely because the objects belong to the same family. The robot agents and controller implementations are under tasks/robots/__init__.py ↗.

Published data and baselines use Sharpa

The released demonstration sets and reported baseline scores use the Sharpa hand. The current dataset and checkpoint release ↗ must not be presented as a matched demonstration set for all four end effectors. Training a different hand requires compatible data, controller binding and a clearly labeled evaluation.

Sharpa has 29 absolute joint targets for one arm/hand and 58 for the bimanual robot. These dimensions are not universal across hands. Read the live action space and ordered joint names for your robot; never pad, truncate or reuse a Sharpa checkpoint without an explicit embodiment adapter.

Changing a hand is a separate experiment

Robot geometry, contact behavior, controller gains and state/action normalization can all change with the end effector. Revalidate the environment reset, mesh loading and success predicates, then record the source revision and hand variant with every result.

Use Policy integration for adapter requirements, Configurations for camera and control contracts, and Data & replay before claiming a demonstration is compatible with the modified robot.
